What's more, the Switch 2 library has only grown since launch, with a great mix of exclusives like The Ocarina of Time and Pokémon Pokopia, alongside plenty of ports and indies, available on the console.

In a recent development, costco is one of the better retailers to buy the AirPods Pro 3 or AirPods 5 from this Black Friday. Not only has the tech giant discounted both pairs of earbuds, but it's also throwing in AppleCare+. The AirPods Pro 3 are $69 off their regular $249 price, and come with two years of Apple's extended warranty coverage, while the AirPods 5 with wireless charging case are $130, down from $149, and include one-year of extended Apple support. With the AirPods Pro 3, a year of AppleCare+ costs $2 per month or $20 annually. For the AirPods 5, the price is $1.49 per month or $15 annually, Either way you're not only saving money by going with Costco, you're also getting a bit of peace of mind with extra coverage.

According to recent reports, you can get the AirPods Pro 3 from Amazon and Best Buy for less money overall ($149 versus $179), but neither firm is including complimentary AppleCare+ coverage like Costco. If you were planning to extend the warranty for your fresh earbuds anyway, Costco has the best offer.

Industry observers note that engadget reviewed both the AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods 5, giving them scores of 90 and 88, respectively. With active noise cancellation now standard across Apple's current AirPods line, you can't really go wrong with either model. One thing to note is there are two different versions of the AirPods 5. The variant Costco has discounted is the one you want to buy if you decide to go with the AirPods 5. It comes with a wireless charging case that offers volume gesture controls and audible Find My features.

It has been revealed that like many other US retailers, Costco has discounted the Oura Ring 5 by $100, bringing the wearable down to $299 and its lowest price yet. All three color options — silver, black and gold — are $100 off, and inclusive of the retailer's exclusive bundle, which adds an extra year of warranty and a second USB-C charging station. Like the Switch 2 bundle, this deal is only available to Costco members.

According to recent reports, the Oura Ring 5 is another Engadget favorite. Senior Editor Daniel Cooper reviewed it earlier this year and a give it a glowing 9 out 10. The fact the Oura Ring 5 is 40 percent smaller than its predecessor, while offering an even better seven days of battery life, make it an easy recommendation for anyone looking to try a smart ring for the first time.

Recent findings suggest that look at you considering a Sonos Arc Ultra. The tech giant's flagship soundbar is $250 off for Black Friday, making it currently $850 instead of its usual eye-watering price of $1100. That price also beats the $900 the Arc Ultra was briefly listed for last month. If you decide to buy a Sonos Sub at the same time, Costco will take an extra $70 off your total transaction. You're still paying $1,500 before tax for both devices, but I imagine there won't be many opportunities to buy a complete Arc Ultra setup for less.

In a recent development, engadget's resident audio guru Billy Steele gave the Arc Ultra a score of 87 back in 2024. The soundbar marked the debut of Sonos' Sound Motion technology, which the manufacturer claimed would improve the Arc's bass performance. In Steele's testing, the soundbar did offer better low-frequency performance, as well as clarity and depth, than its predecessor. The Arc is pricey, but if you don't want to deal with a multi-speaker setup, and all the wires that come with one, the Sonos Arc Ultra at $850 is one of the best high-end soundbars you can buy. And even if you're not a CostCo member, Sonos' own Black Friday sale has the Arc Ultra available for the same $850 price, along with a bunch of other solid discounts on the company's speakers and headphones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chile’s national competition authority, Fiscalía Nacional Económica (FNE), has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Apple, accusing the organization of abusing its dominant position in iOS app distribution and in-app purchases. Here are the details.

As reported by Reuters, Chile’s competition watchdog is seeking an $80 million fine against Apple, along with a court order requiring a series of changes to the company’s App Store policies.

In its complaint, the FNE indicates (translation ours):.

The defendant has violated Article 3, paragraphs one and two, subsection (b), of Decree Law 211 by abusing its dominant position through practices that prevent, restrict, or hinder free competition, or have the potential to do so, in the markets for app distribution and the distribution of paid digital goods within apps, both on the iOS operating system nationwide, from at least 2019 to the present day.

The FNE goes on to say that Apple forbids both sideloading and alternative app marketplaces, requires app developers to exclusively use the manufacturer’s In-App Purchase system to sell digital goods and services within their apps, and restricts their ability to inform users about or direct them to alternative payment methods.

It then goes on to claim that “these anticompetitive practices have allowed the defendant to ensure that the App Store is the only channel for downloading apps,” adding that this “has led to a degradation of the consumer experience and allowed Apple to secure profits that it would not obtain without such practices.”.

Throughout the 50-page filing, the FNE draws on regulatory and judicial precedents from other jurisdictions, some involving ongoing disputes, to support its arguments that Apple’s restrictions are anticompetitive and that its privacy and security objectives can be achieved through less restrictive means.

Sources indicate that that includes Apple’s agreement with Brazil’s competition authority, the European Union’s Digital Markets Act, the Epic Games v. Apple ruling in Australia, regulatory and judicial developments in Japan, and the lifting of anti-steering restrictions in the US.

At one point, the FNE even suggests that Apple knowingly maintained anticompetitive practices in the country, despite regulatory and judicial developments elsewhere:.

Industry observers note that furthermore, there is evidence suggesting that the defendant was aware of the unlawfulness of its conduct, given the existence of precedents in other jurisdictions involving facts similar to those alleged in this complaint, which demonstrate the anticompetitive nature of the alleged practices. Nevertheless, Apple decided to maintain its restrictions in Chile, as well as in other jurisdictions where it has not been compelled to remove them or has not agreed with the relevant authority to eliminate or modify them.

After presenting its case, the FNE asks Chile’s antitrust court to:.

Additionally, the FNE asks the court to require Apple to implement these measures “in good faith, such that it may not impose any other technical or contractual restrictions, or commercial conditions, that undermine their purpose,” to cease the alleged anticompetitive practices, and to cover the legal costs of the proceedings.

It also leaves room for the court to impose any additional measures it deems appropriate, particularly those aimed at facilitating access to alternative channels for app distribution and the sale of digital goods.

9to5Mac has reached out to Apple for comment and will enhancement this post if the manufacturer responds.

You can read the FNE’s full complaint here (in Spanish).

Apple Brings Its iPhone Broadcasting to Formula 1 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track.
  • Using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty.
  • But compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when you watch a Formula 1 race on TV, the screen is packed with lap times, driver stats and real-time video from inside the cars and around the track. During the Las Vegas Grand Prix race, some of those views were captured with iPhone Pro phones and transmitted in real time over T-Mobile’s 5G network.

Using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. In May, Apple broadcast a Major League Soccer game shot with iPhones strapped to professional lenses, following it up with a Major League Baseball game in September using its own camera hardware,.

But compared to a ballpark, F1 ratchets up the complexity, especially in Las Vegas. At the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the race track snakes 3.9 miles through the city’s downtown core. Its route includes the famed Strip (South Las Vegas Boulevard), where most of the major hotels are.

According to recent reports, “We control everything on baseball, so we can do whatever we want there,” said Royce Dickerson, executive producer of live sports at Apple TV. “We did 14 iPhones on top of our normal camera complement” during the baseball broadcast. He noted that 10 of those were connected via T-Mobile’s 5G wireless network.

But integrating iPhone cameras into an F1 broadcast, even for the sport’s US broadcaster, is more of a challenge. “I’ve been doing TV production for 20-plus years,” said Dickerson, “and the scale of their operation is unlike anything I’ve seen before.”.

According to recent reports, because F1 has agreements with other camera partners, Dickerson did not specify how many iPhones were set up around the track. Neither Apple nor T-Mobile explained where the iPhones were placed in order to capture the speedy F1 vehicles racing around the Vegas Strip. I suspect they were likely deployed in more conventional environments for smartphone cameras, like the team garages and roving to catch celebrities in the paddock area and in the stands, though the iPhone setups wirelessly broadcasting footage at earlier sporting events means they could be easily placed in many locations on and above the streets.

It has been revealed that “You really have to work hard to earn the fans’ attention [and] that viewing experience,” mentioned Dickerson. “How are you getting your fans closer to their favorite athlete, to their favorite driver, to their team, to the personalities that surround the sport?”.

Sources indicate that in the T-Mobile zone at the Sphere – an area sponsored by the carrier and open to T-Mobile customers – at least 10 iPhone cameras were used to cover a stage where concerts played between events. That number is based on a diagram shared during a tour of T-Mobile’s Tech Trailer, where the company’s event coordinators stay on top of things like crowd movements and line lengths.

Dean Locke, executive director of broadcast, media and race operations at Formula 1, sees the combination of multiple cameras streaming wirelessly over 5G as an essential component to the Las Vegas race.

“If we just did cameras at a low level, the fences and track, we haven’t done a very good job,” said Locke. “How can we open up stages, concerts and all of the activities? Each race has a real kind of personality to it. You can only [capture that personality] with huge amounts of cameras, huge amounts of technology.”.

If Apple is using iPhones to record live sports, are they recording any of that footage using spatial video for viewing in the Vision Pro? Imagine getting a track-level view of a group of Formula 1 cars speeding past at 200 miles per hour with Apple’s depth effect. “[There’s] nothing at this time I can say about it,” remarked Dickerson.

It has been revealed that editors’ note: Jeff Carlson’s travel costs for the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix were covered by T-Mobile. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

  • German robotics firm NEURA Robotics has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Government of Aragón and agri-food group Costa Group to open a NEURA Gym in Aragón by mid-2027.
  • Sources indicate that german robotics company NEURA Robotics prepares to open a robot training centre in Aragón, Spain, by mid-2027, it mentioned on Thursday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Representatives of NEURA Robotics, the Government of Aragón and Costa Group sign the memorandum of understanding.

German robotics firm NEURA Robotics has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Government of Aragón and agri-food group Costa Group to open a NEURA Gym in Aragón by mid-2027. The partners strategy to invest in the double-digit millions of euros, with NEURA leading, and to add a zone for testing robots in real settings.

Sources indicate that german robotics company NEURA Robotics prepares to open a robot training centre in Aragón, Spain, by mid-2027, it mentioned on Thursday. It has signed a memorandum of understanding with the regional government and Costa Group, an Aragonese meat and agri-food group.

Recent findings suggest that the partners proposal to invest in the “double-digit millions of euros”, with NEURA taking the lead. They did not give an exact figure.

The site will be one of NEURA’s Gyms, where companies train robots on real tasks before putting them to work. Firms will bring their own processes, test them on different robots and check how well they perform.

Through NEURA’s Neuraverse platform, companies can keep the robot skills they develop private or license them to others for a fee.

“A manufacturer that develops a valuable skill should benefit when others use it,” said David Reger, NEURA’s founder and chief executive.

Costa Group will supply real problems from its farms and factories. The first projects will aim to cut physically demanding and repetitive work, before moving into logistics, cars and manufacturing. The University of Zaragoza will add research and train staff.

Industry observers note that the partners also plan a “Physical AI Model Zone”, where robots can be tested in real working settings. Its scope and locations are still to be agreed, and any testing in public areas will need permits.

NEURA raised up to $1.4B in June, partly to expand its Gyms. It has since bought two companies. In Spain, Barcelona’s THEKER raised €73M in June for factory robots that learn on the job.

This tracks bombs and missiles across more than 200 Air Force locations worldwide. One of Reuters' sources said "A breach here is a massive deal.".

#4355. Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1901 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your tech giant.
  • Industry observers note that do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a manufacturer call contained in a federal lawsuit.
  • Sources indicate that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your tech giant. Right now. Or else.

Industry observers note that do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a manufacturer call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”.

Sources indicate that shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”.

Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted. “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform. “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”.

President Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “convinced” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.

Fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.

It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official says. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”.

Documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.

“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.

“It’s just straight-up coercion,” says Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The tech giant starts making decisions not based on what’s best for the company in the short or long term, what’s best for shareholders, but what’s best for politics and what the government is demanding.”.

“That’s not what you want from any organization,” he adds. “When you’re talking about the world’s most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that’s a huge problem.”.

In a recent development, representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

It has been revealed that the parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the company’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office.

During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.

Industry observers note that at the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, says the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times.) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “a horrible, horrible thing.” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration stated it was renegotiating the deals.

Industry observers note that the same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s new CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing’s military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.

Sources indicate that two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted, “The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.”.

Tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change, Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.

“The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background, and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”.

Neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the manufacturer. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told The Wall Street Journal. “I remarked, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”.

Sources indicate that “I should’ve asked for more. It was so easy,” Trump later recalled.

According to recent reports, according to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the Latest York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the organization’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.

Then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he said, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”.

Intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the manufacturer,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.

But they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the organization. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”.

On August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and said. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”.

Inside the tech giant, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”.

Recent findings suggest that not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted. “Who would not want to make deals like that?”.

Deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump unveiled that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang. The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I noted, if I’m going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.

In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”.

Sources indicate that in court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the company “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”.

The attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones remarked on the tech giant’s quarterly earnings call that it did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The Newly introduced York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.

It has been revealed that “Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this manufacturer, not even a little bit,” Huang said during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported. “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The suit suggests that the iPhone maker is trying to “compete unfairly by any means available.”.

It has been revealed that openAI has filed a major lawsuit against Apple that accuses the iPhone maker of stealing trade secrets, according to a report by Financial Times. The folks behind ChatGPT have also accused Apple of "coercing and threatening" suppliers who work with both companies. OpenAI indicates Apple is trying to "compete unfairly by any means available", which includes encouraging employees to store corporate files on personal devices and cloud storage accounts.

Industry observers note that the complaint is filled with flowery language that suggests "Apple set quite a trap for employees" and that "bright young minds thought they would work in Cupertino. Instead they were joining Hotel California: you can check out any time you like, but you can never leave.".

Sources indicate that this follows a suit issued by Apple against OpenAI that accused the AI manufacturer of stealing secret trade information. This was filed after OpenAI acquired an entity called io, which is a studio led by Apple's former design chief Jony Ive. At that point, Apple called ChatGPT "rotten to its core." Now it looks like OpenAI is getting involved in a bit of tit for tat.

Apple has yet to comment on today's lawsuit, but it wasn't that long ago in which the two companies were partnered up to bring ChatGPT to iPhones. Now OpenAI is prepping its own line of hardware products that could directly compete with Apple.

To that end, the firm has accused a former employee of returning to Apple and sharing details about product aims and suppliers. This is pretty much the exact same thing Apple accused OpenAI of doing in its suit.

That filing names several former Apple employees and notes they "surreptitiously accessed and downloaded dozens of Apple's confidential hardware-related files, including voluminous, detailed information about unreleased products, engineering presentations, technical specifications and proprietary project data.".

Sources indicate that in any event, the courts will have to settle this whole thing. We'll keep you posted as these two suits make their way through the legal system.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A carpet cleaner may not be your first thought for a Black Friday purchase, but it’s actually a great time to buy one, since one of my favorite fresh cleaners I’ve tested is on sale. The Bissell Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner is $85 at Amazon, down from its usual $130 price. That’s a $45 savings and, according to Amazon, its lowest price in 365 days. That’s considerably cheaper than the Shark StainForce, which goes for around $200 and is $130 for Black Friday.

The Bissell Little Green cleaner offers tons of cleaning power in a small package at a reasonable price, though there are one or two catches regarding portability and setup that are worth knowing about before you decide which one to buy.

The Bissell Little Green Mini is a powerful portable spot cleaner. / CNET/Ajay Kumar.

According to recent reports, the Bissell Little Green Mini is a corded portable spot cleaner, but it’s still lightweight at 7 pounds. Setup is definitely a little more involved, with a clean water tank that you need to mix cleaning solution into and the need to have an AC outlet somewhere in the area. The trade-off is a significantly deeper, more powerful cleaning than what you get with a handheld battery-powered spot cleaner like the Shark StainForce. Using the Little Green on the toughest and oldest dried stains left by my pukey old man cat left me impressed with just how deeply it cleaned my carpets. The pristine result makes this corded cleaner well worth the extra setup, and even at full price ($130), you won’t find fault with its power or portability.

At $85, its lowest price in a year on Amazon, the Bissell Little Green Mini is an easy buy if you have pets and carpet.

Shark StainForce cleaning a stain off my carpet. / Ajay Kumar/CNET.

In a recent development, the Shark StainForce is a unique handheld vacuum because it doesn’t just clean dry messes — it’s primarily intended to remove stains and wet messes. It resembles other handheld vacuums, but comes with a caddy and a custom Shark stain cleaner that mixes a deep cleaner and oxy cleaner in the spray bottle to lift stains.

Sources indicate that it works incredibly well — I was blown away by how easily it lifted the worst messes off my white carpets. It removed yellow cat puke stains, wine stains and tomato sauce off both the carpet and couch. It works equally well for older dried stains and wet stains, using a mix of the stain cleaner spray and agitation with the included rubber scrubbing brush head that suctions up the mess at the same time. There’s also a smaller nozzle-brush cleaner included for tight spots.

The StainForce will suction up dry waste like cat hair and chunks of half-digested cat food, but the waste tank is fairly small, and it’s not really meant for dry cleaning of a large area due to the limited battery life.

The tank will also need to be cleaned out and dried after every use because wet messes will fester and smell if left too long. With all that remarked, this is the only portable spot cleaner I’ve seen with the design and usability of a handheld vacuum, which makes it an excellent choice if your primary need is portable spot cleaning. The $200 price may sound steep, but I’ve never seen a compact cleaner as good at tackling such tough stains.

Recent findings suggest that I love the Shark StainForce for its service as a grab-and-go cleaner. It’s cordless, it lives in its caddy ready to go, and for a fresh spill I can spray, scrub, and suction in under a minute with no setup at all. I’ve used it on my cats’ worst messes, including hairballs, vomit from eating too fast, and dirty paws tracked in from the litter box. It works remarkably well for something so small and it’s still the go-to cleaner for my wife and I. The dual-spray bottle that comes with it does an incredible job of lifting stains, even from my white carpet.

Here I am scrubbing away with the StainForce powered on. You can still see some stain, but it’s going away.

The Little Green Mini is a different kind of machine, and that difference shows in the results. On a day when my cats were in rare form and decided to throw up on the bedroom carpet three times in a row, I knew a small portable cleaner like the StainForce wouldn’t cut it, not with the sheer quantity of debris they’d left behind.

I pulled the Bissell Little Green, which, worth acknowledging, is corded. That means more setup: fill the 16-ounce clean tank with water and the included Oxy formula, plug in the 12-foot cord, and work within reach of the cord and its 4-foot hose. It’s still light at just 7 pounds, and it has a useful handle for moving it from room to room.

Industry observers note that the StainForce, by contrast, has no clean tank at all. You spray from a separate bottle and only a tiny dirty-water collection tank of under 5 ounces, with about 15 minutes of battery before it needs a recharge. The Mini’s clean and dirty tanks (16 and 13.5 ounces) are much bigger, and because it’s plugged in, it never runs out of power mid-clean.

That proved to be the lifesaver in cleaning my cat’s horrible messes. The Bissell generously saturated the stain with its built-in sprayer that can dispense water and cleaning solution straight from the hose. The hose digs in deep, rinsing and pulling stains, mess and dirt from deep out of the carpet layers. The larger chunks were safely suctioned into the dirty tank, along with the used water.

Recent findings suggest that what I can say is that it did an excellent job of deep-cleaning stains from the carpet — noticeably deeper than the StainForce. It completely removed our cat’s mess, with no trace left behind, though our carpets were left a little moist. My wife’s verdict was that she’s never seen the carpets so clean before and she audibly wondered if it was worth investing in a full-size carpet cleaner because clearly the StainForce and vacuuming aren’t cutting it.

It has been revealed that if you want the fastest possible cleanup for a fresh spill, get the Shark StainForce; it’s hard to beat a cordless cleaner with zero setup. For a smaller mess that I just want to get off my carpet, the StainForce more than does its job. But if your problem is stains that have soaked into the carpet, the Bissell Little Green Mini is the better cleaner, and at $85 on Black Friday — its lowest Amazon price in a year — it’s $45 less than the StainForce right now. It’s the one I’d buy for a house with pets, kids and carpets where you don’t want a substantial and bulky carpet cleaner and don’t want to worry about running out of charge for a bigger mess.

According to recent reports, verizon is in talks to buy Fidium, a fibre broadband operator owned by Searchlight Capital and BCI, for about $6B including debt, the Financial Times reported. A deal could come within weeks, as Verizon tries to win more home internet customers after buying Frontier.

Verizon is in talks to buy US fibre broadband operator Fidium for about $6B including debt, the Financial Times reported on Friday, according to Bloomberg.

Fidium is owned by Searchlight Capital Partners and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI). A deal could come in the coming weeks, the FT said, though another bidder may emerge and the talks may not lead to a takeover.

Recent findings suggest that verizon declined to comment. Fidium did not immediately respond to Bloomberg.

The Illinois-based company sells fibre internet in more than 20 US states. It was called Consolidated Communications until last year, when it renamed itself after its fibre brand. Searchlight and BCI agreed to take it private in 2023 in a $3.1B deal including debt.

Industry observers note that verizon has been buying fibre networks to catch up with rivals in home internet. Earlier this year, it closed its $9.6B purchase of Frontier Communications.

Sources indicate that growth has still been slow. Verizon added 314,000 broadband customers in the third quarter, below analysts’ estimates, even as it signed up twice as many upcoming phone customers as expected.

According to recent reports, chief executive Dan Schulman told investors that customers increasingly prefer fibre to 5G-powered home internet. Since taking over last year, Schulman has cut retail jobs and argued that SpaceX would need up to $500B to match Verizon’s mobile network.

#4345. Restricted NVIDIA chips were installed at a Chinese data center linked to Alice Huang

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Restricted NVIDIA chips were installed at a Chinese data center linked to Alice Huang

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bloomberg traced the lineage of one GB300 server rack to Gigabyte Technology.
  • It has been revealed that well, this is awkward.
  • Recent findings suggest that A single GB300 NVL72 unit houses 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Grace processors, and can weigh about 3,300 pounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bloomberg traced the lineage of one GB300 server rack to Gigabyte Technology.

It has been revealed that well, this is awkward. Bloomberg reports it may have found evidence of a link between a Chinese data center with NVIDIA Blackwell hardware and Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the controversy surrounding Jensen Huang's brief resignation from the organization. Looking through documents two different firms submitted to Chinese regulators, the outlet found mention of GB300 NVL72 and GB200 server racks at the Yangtze River Delta Project in Shanghai. One of the companies, Shanghai Shuoyao, listed a GB300 NVL72 rack as collateral to secure an approximately $14 million loan from the Shanghai Innovation Bank.

Recent findings suggest that A single GB300 NVL72 unit houses 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Grace processors, and can weigh about 3,300 pounds. US export rules require a license to ship these Blackwell systems to China. As Bloomberg notes, Jensen Huang once claimed GB300 racks are too major to smuggle. It's unclear how the GB300 and GB200 units made their way to the Shanghai facility, which may eventually house as many as 800,000 servers.

According to recent reports, however, Bloomberg was able to partly track the lineage of the GB300 unit. By putting the serial of the rack into a public warranty database, the outlet was able to trace it back to Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology, which PC gamers will know as one of NVIDIA's many add-in board partners. Like other NVIDIA AIBs, Gigabyte buys GPU chips from the company that it then uses to manufacture graphics cards for consumers and servers for enterprise customers.

It has been revealed that gigabyte declined to answer Bloomberg's questions about what company or party originally bought the GB300 rack. A spokesperson told the outlet it "conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations," adding, "all transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time.".

Industry observers note that shanghai Shuoyao, the organization that offered a GB300 as collateral, has ties with Megaspeed. Alice Huang took a controlling stake in the Singaporean cloud computing company in 2023 before leaving it in August 2025. Earlier this month, Shanghai Shuoyao noted it was one of Megaspeed's service providers, but described its relationship with the company as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation.".

According to Bloomberg, Megaspeed used renderings of the Yangtze River Delta Project in a presentation it shared with investors in 2024. The deck did not list China as the location of the data center. Bloomberg notes it does not have evidence that Megaspeed directly diverted NVIDIA chips to the data center, and the organization denies any wrongdoing. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules. NVIDIA did not immediately respond to Engadget's comment request.

According to recent reports, alice Huang appears to have had a number of other ties to the Yangtze River Delta Project. Most notably, through Kang Wei, the man The Newly introduced York Times reports was often introduced as her husband and appears to have had ties with China's Ministry of State Security. Bloomberg found him listed as the president of the facility. The publication also found evidence of servers containing NVIDIA's earlier Hopper-generation chips inside the Yangtze River Delta Project. Those GPUs are also illegal to ship to China without permission from the US government.

Jensen Huang is set to testify publicly before Congress on December 3 at 10AM ET.

Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime’s bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005.

In a recent development, it is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and introduced a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron’s schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City—heroes, all of them!—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator, against which there appeared to be no defense.

It has been revealed that and then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: “Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost.” The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that and how do we remember those Autobots who joined the Allspark so that we could live in freedom? Why, we celebrate Black Friday through commerce and buying things—just like Optimus Prime would have wanted! Below is a list of the finest deals we could locate, in a broad range of categories. The pricing is current as of (checks watch) right now, where “right now” equals the timestamp on this story’s publication. Peruse the list and see if anything in it jumps out at you—we’ll attempt to refresh it at least once throughout the day with updated pricing and stuff.

If the darkness of the Black Friday story threatens to overwhelm your soul, fear not. Optimus Prime was succeeded by Rodimus Prime, who defeated the darkness and brought hope back to all Cybertron. (We don’t talk about the brief Ultra Magnus-led Prime Interregnal Period.) Even Optimus Prime himself wouldn’t stay dead for very long—his own glorious and perhaps narratively inevitable resurrection would occur not that long after. Indeed, we will be celebrating those grand events in just a couple of days, on Cybertron Monday (or just “Cyber Monday” for short), with more shopping!

In a recent development, read on for our Black Friday deals. (You can also check over on Wired for more Black Friday deals and stuff—they usually run a longer list than we do!) Enjoy!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The feature could mirror the Siri mode Apple added in iOS 27.

Samsung's Galaxy S26 phones already ship with Google's Android AI features and Perplexity, and the phone maker is reportedly layering in even more AI for next year's Galaxy S27 devices. Based on code strings in One UI 9.5 Beta 1, Android Authority writes that Samsung is adding a upcoming "Vision" mode to Galaxy phones' camera app that could duplicate some of the use cases for Siri mode in iOS 27.

Industry observers note that vision will apparently be offered alongside the app's other modes, and primarily acts as a way to point your camera at something and ask AI about it. According to Android Authority, the camera mode will display an AI-written summary of whatever you're looking at, along with tappable keywords, suggested actions, a text extraction tool, an "Ask" button that sends the scene to Gemini and a "Translate" button that hands it off to Samsung's AI Vision app.

Recent findings suggest that samsung's phones already offer a way to open Google's Gemini Live feature to have a live conversation about whatever you're looking at, and even before that, Samsung experimented with multimodal AI features through Bixby. Funnily enough, Android Authority writes that the AI Vision app this fresh camera feature connects to is actually built on the bones of Bixby Vision, the camera capabilities of Samsung's in-house AI assistant.

In a recent development, vision also sounds similar to the Siri mode Apple added to the Camera app in iOS 27. Siri mode basically freed the iPhone's Visual Intelligence features from its Camera Control button and brought them into an app people spend a lot more time in. Samsung's Vision feature doesn't sound like it's adding anything new to the concept, but if it makes it even easier to ask AI about the world around you, maybe that will be worth it to some users.

Recent findings suggest that samsung hasn't revealed this feature, and sometimes software appears in betas that never make it to the final release. If Samsung does launch this new Vision feature, it will likely be alongside the Galaxy S27 lineup early next year.

Which Samsung folding phone is right for you? Galaxy Z Fold 8, Ultra, or Flip 8

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that folding phones are entering a new chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start.
  • Samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar.
  • Sources indicate that each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that folding phones are entering a new chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start. In this guide, we’ll take a look at some of the most important questions to answer when buying a foldable, and dissect how Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 fit the bill to figure out which is the best for you, especially if you’re interested in one this holiday season.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

Samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar. The Galaxy Z Flip 8 continues the lineup of clamshell-style foldables, offering a form factor similar to that of a classic flip phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, meanwhile, is designed to be a normal smartphone on the outside, hiding a tablet within. Finally, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the newly introduced kid on the block, offering a compact outer display that opens up to a media-friendly, wider inner panel.

Sources indicate that each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs. Here’s a quick rundown of the key details on each device:.

Starting with the displays, the book-style Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra both provide outer displays that are fully usable as standard smartphones, while the inner display is useful for multitasking, media, or just getting more space for reading a website or e-book. Samsung’s top-tier specs deliver performance for everything you’d need, with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy powering everything from demanding games or media-editing apps to day-to-day use.

In a recent development, with each Samsung foldable, you’re getting a fully capable smartphone, but finding the one that’s best for you is a matter of picking your most vital priorities. Cameras, battery life, content consumption, and size are some of the most important points to consider, so let’s take a look one-by-one.

According to recent reports, when it comes to cameras, foldables have a tough time. There’s only so much physical space to fit the camera sensors and, with cameras, having more space generally results in a battery overall camera.

That said, the best camera on a Samsung foldable is undoubtedly on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

Sources indicate that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a 200MP main camera that’s similar to the Galaxy S26 Ultra, while it also packs a 50MP ultrawide and something neither of the others offer, a telephoto lens. The 10MP telephoto shooter captures faraway subjects at 3x optical zoom, meaning you’re not giving up on quality when you zoom in. Two 10MP cameras can be found on the displays, with neither sacrificing quality for an under-display look.

Sources indicate that runner-up here is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which offers a pair of 50MP cameras for wide and ultrawide shots. You can get 2x optical-quality zoom out of the main sensor to still get a good zoom shot, while the main camera still offers good quality and Samsung’s best camera features including 2x optical-quality zoom and the subject-tracking My FanCam.

The Galaxy Z Flip 8 may not have the best camera hardware, but what it lacks in hardware it makes up for in flexibility. This is definitely the best form factor of the bunch for using the foldable design as a tripod for capturing clips. All three devices also use their foldable nature to let you capture full-quality selfies using the rear cameras, which always have better quality than the 10MP dedicated front-facing cameras.

Here’s where specs on paper can tell a different story compared to real life.

Sources indicate that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra may offer the biggest battery of the bunch at 5,000 mAh, but its battery life is on par with the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both foldables are designed to last you through a full day, though sticking to the outer display only on the Fold 8 Ultra may bring you slightly better battery life overall.

In either case, you’re also getting 45W fast charging over USB-C, granting you speedy recharging if your device happens to get low through the course of a busy day. These are also “Qi2 Ready,” meaning you can use magnetic wireless chargers if you use a compatible magnetic case.

One of the most key things you’ll want to ask yourself when buying a foldable phone is why you want to opt for a foldable in the first place, and each of these devices gives a different answer.

Industry observers note that the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a productivity powerhouse, delivering more space on its inner display for you to get work done through the web, apps, and more. You can run up to three apps at once on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s display, as well as floating apps, and more.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 is great for media consumption. The wider aspect ratio is perfect for watching videos, playing games, reading books, and more, all while still giving you plenty of space for productivity just like the Ultra.

Galaxy Z Flip 8, meanwhile, is all about giving you a more compact device. The outer display lets you swiftly reply to messages or keep up with directions, while you can unfold it to do everything you want to on a normal phone. Close it up to more easily stow it away in your pocket or your bag.

In a recent development, if you are moving into a upcoming Galaxy foldable, the good news is that you don’t have to start from scratch. Thanks to Samsung’s Smart Switch app, you can easily transfer supported content including pictures, contacts, messages, and more from an older Galaxy phone, another Android phone, or even an iPhone over to a Galaxy foldable. Apps, messages, photos, and more can all make the move wirelessly, without the need of a cable.

You can get the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra, and Flip 8 from your favorite carriers and retailers, but Best Buy is one of the best places to score a great deal with solid trade-in values and deep discounts around Black Friday and throughout the holiday season.

Five recent tech outages were not due to AI; the next round will be

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.
  • That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….
  • Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five major tech outages in quick succession earlier this month led to speculation that they were connected, with some inevitably believing them to be AI-related.

That wasn’t the case, but the US Director of National Intelligence is one of a number of experts warning that we should expect AI-powered outages in the near future ….

Earlier this month saw five tech outages, one after the other. A widespread Microsoft 365 outage occurred when two unrelated problems coincided. The next day saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication glitch affecting all air traffic control centers. A few days later, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Many Apple services went offline later the same week, with retail stores also affected. Finally, United Airlines had its own widespread IT outage that grounded a significant number of flights.

Each had their own unrelated causes, with the White House stating that rumors of an AI-facilitated systemic attack by a hostile state were false.

It has been revealed that however, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that we should expect future tech outages as a result of attacks facilitated by AI-discovered vulnerabilities. CNBC reports him issuing the warning on CNN’s State of the Union.

The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road.

You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot.

We already saw an example of this last month when a vulnerability discovered in PHP saw a significant number of websites being taken offline.

Microsoft President Brad Smith claims it isn’t just a question of bad actors exploiting vulnerabilities discovered by AI, but companies rushing to patch these may inadvertently cause systems to fail, as Newsweek reports.

What AI did earlier this year was basically make it much easier for people to find vulnerabilities in code, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.

Especially when you have older infrastructure, especially when you’re trying to patch at such a pace, especially when you have to go so fast that you can’t take as much time to test what you’re changing in the code, you do increase the risk of something going wrong.

Major IT failures look set to be a routine event in the coming weeks and months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to a upcoming report, Samsung’s next “Galaxy Watch 10” won’t be releasing in 2027 with the manufacturer moving to a bi-yearly release schedule for its smartwatches.

ETNews reports that Samsung will not have a fresh Galaxy Watch model releasing in 2027, a series that would have likely been called “Galaxy Watch 10.” The reason, the report suggests, is that Samsung is “undertaking a structural overhaul to strengthen profitability” (translated) following two quarters in a row of losses in its mobile division.

Samsung has released a new Galaxy Watch every year since 2018, with 2021’s Galaxy Watch 4 marking the switch to Wear OS.

In a recent development, the new schedule will apparently see new Galaxy Watch releases every other year, pushing the next release into 2028. The report goes on to mention that Galaxy Watch is part of a “mature phase” of the smartwatch market, and that Galaxy Watch 9 sales “fell short of expectations” likely due in part to its higher price point.

Apparently, Samsung aims new Galaxy Watch software updates next year as well as “enhancement of healthcare features.” The Galaxy Fit 4 fitness tracker is also expected in 2027, with Dealabs reporting that the tracker will be priced at €79.90 in Europe, a slight price hike over the previous release.

One of the most dramatic shifts in the AI landscape is the emergence of intelligent agents that can use iPhone and Mac apps in order to carry out tasks on our behalf.

Industry observers note that we can already use third-party chatbots in this way, and we know Apple is working hard to turn Siri AI into an agent. However, before the firm even gets the chance, banks are already blocking them, and this may be just the start ….

It has been revealed that the science fiction promise of AI has always been to be able to tell a computer what we want done and have the task carried out for us automatically. That’s starting to turn into a reality with the emergence of AI agents.

We’ve already seen Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, and Muse gain agent capabilities, and Apple is expected to bring these to Siri AI at some point next year.

In a recent development, earlier this month, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman noted that the company ultimately wants to go in this direction and may add these abilities next year. CEO John Ternus has reportedly been pushing Craig Federighi for faster software development, with specific mention of “moving beyond necessary improvements to Siri,” which seems likely to mean agentic capabilities.

Last week also saw a since-deleted Apple job listing detailing aims for autonomous AI agents.

According to recent reports, we’ve already seen some of the ways in which this can go wrong, and we recently outlined three significant risks. Wired reports that banks are now responding to these by either blocking AI agents or warning customers that using them can be dangerous.

Wells Fargo even goes as far as using capitals in its latest terms, stating that it will not be responsible for the consequences.

Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK.

We can likely expect similar pushback in sectors like online shopping as companies fear high returns costs and other consequences from mistakes by AI agents.

Sources indicate that personally, I don’t give any AI agents access to any of my banking or other financial services, considering the risks to be too high. I don’t see my position changing any time soon.

Industry observers note that what’s your take? Would you trust an AI agent with access to your bank accounts? If not, would Apple launching agentic capabilities for Siri AI change your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Fitbit Air is a simple screenless fitness tracker, but it can do a bit more, and now someone has built an app that lets the Air buzz your wrist when phone notifications come through.
  • The era of vibe-coding has been very quickly bringing ideas to reality, and these newly introduced Fitbit Air notification apps are a great example.
  • In a recent development, “Air Relay” is the result of a developer managing to reverse-engineer a way to control haptics on the Fitbit Air via Bluetooth without affecting Google Health sync.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Fitbit Air is a simple screenless fitness tracker, but it can do a bit more, and now someone has built an app that lets the Air buzz your wrist when phone notifications come through.

The era of vibe-coding has been very quickly bringing ideas to reality, and these newly introduced Fitbit Air notification apps are a great example.

In a recent development, “Air Relay” is the result of a developer managing to reverse-engineer a way to control haptics on the Fitbit Air via Bluetooth without affecting Google Health sync. “Cuff” uses the same method while also showing health stats if you don’t want to use Google Health.

The idea here is pretty simple. You can have apps on your phone ping your Fitbit Air as you choose. “Air Relay” lets you pick select apps and even change the vibration pattern or strength based on the app. You can set “Quiet hours” to prevent notifications while you’re sleeping, and there’s a WhatsApp-specific setting that lets you only get notifications from specific groups or people. A “Find My Air” setting uses Bluetooth strength you help you track down a lost tracker.

While a big part of the appeal of Fitbit Air is its screenless, disconnected nature, having the option to set up alerts for important apps or contacts is certainly a useful option.

“Air Relay” is free on Google Play, and Fitbit Air is available for $99.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has unveiled that disgraced CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated to the role, effective immediately. The company’s share price jumped more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also making significant gains.

It remarked that the board voted unanimously in favor of reinstatement despite its recent statement that it had no intention of doing so ….

Huang’s affair with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy became the main headline news in the tech press after coming to light at the end of last month. The Newly introduced York Times broke the story on October 29, citing it then as “a close relationship.” Nvidia initially denied that the relationship was anything out of the ordinary.

Sources indicate that that changed on November 8 when Huang publicly admitted to the affair. Nvidia’s shares dropped 5%, and the tech giant’s board of directors opened an independent investigation. Further details emerged over the following days. Things got even worse when the same paper reported that Huang had also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him.

That led to Huang being fired resigning on November 12.

Recent findings suggest that money over country. This is government intervention.

In a recent development, despite putting the firm at enormous risk and initially lying to its board of directors, there were calls in some quarters for Huang to be reinstated. He responded by saying that he would be “honored” to return if asked to do so.

The board of directors, however, mentioned that it had no intention of inviting him back.

Nvidia’s chair Harvey Jones noted: “The board does not intend to reinstate him.”.

That changed today, with the company making the announcement in a press release.

Nvidia today confirmed that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” noted Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Organization. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a upcoming industrial revolution,” mentioned Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”.

As previously unveiled, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The company’s stock price jumped by more than 30% in response, with the rest of the market also up per Yahoo Finance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AirTag-like trackers for Android and iPhone are everywhere nowadays, but Kodak’s new SlideTag steps it up with a built-in E-Ink display that can show off your photos, widgets, and more along with being able to track down your items.

In a recent development, compatible with both the Android Find Hub and Apple Find My networks, the Kodak SlideTag is a tracker inspired by the golden era of Kodak photography. The tracker is built by Reto, the same firm that built the Kodak Chamera keychain digital camera.

Industry observers note that slideTag’s premise is relatively simple. You get a tracker with an E-Ink display and a frame in one of eight styles inspired by classic 35mm slides. Those styles are sold in a blind box format, meaning you don’t know what you’re getting until you open the box (unless you buy the full set). There’s also a ninth style that only shows up in one out of every 64 boxes.

It has been revealed that the E-Ink display can show six-color versions of your photos, or it can display things like lists, calendars, and more. There’s enough storage on the tracker for a 12-photo slideshow, synced through the Kodak Memory Link app on Android and iOS.

Industry observers note that connect instantly via Bluetooth to the KODAK Memory Link App. From live slideshows and custom QR codes to countdowns and dual-network tracking with Apple Find My and Google’s Find Hub, the KODAK SlideTag seamlessly integrates retro aesthetics into your everyday carry.

Kodak SlideTag is available today from Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that the best Apple accessories share a distinct DNA: immaculate industrial design, lightweight ergonomics, tactile physical precision, and friction-free performance that feels native from minute one. Launched globally this fall, the RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo iO pair premium materials and bleeding-edge optics with the one thing Mac and iPhone owners actually want from a display accessory — plug it in, and it works.

In a recent development, rayNeo isn’t a small player making a big claim here. The company took the No. 1 spot in global AR smart glasses shipments across the first half of 2026, with 24.8% market share according to IDC and 23.9% according to Counterpoint Research.

Its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is live now through November 30, with the flagship GT Max at $335 (down from $429), the lighter GT at $249 (down from $329), and the camera-free iO smart glasses at $389 (down from $499). Everything is available on RayNeo.com and Amazon US.

Watching a movie on your iPhone is convenient, but craning your neck for a comfortable view is hardly cinematic. Having a premium AR display in sunglasses form, without packing a bulky mixed-reality headset or computing puck, opens up entirely latest possibilities.

It has been revealed that the RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo GT connect to your device over a single USB-C cable. Instead of clunky goggles, the GT Series puts a massive virtual display — 59 degrees of field of view on GT Max, to be exact — into a sleek, understated sunglasses design that blends into coffee shops and airport lounges at just 68 to 78 grams. That single USB-C connection carries uncompressed video and powers the glasses directly: no secondary battery packs to carry, no charging anxiety, and zero wireless lag.

It has been revealed that one thing to check before you buy: the glasses need a device that outputs video over USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode). That covers the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, Macs from 2015 onward with USB-C, iPad from the 10th generation on, and USB-C handhelds like the Steam Deck. The iPhone 16e, 17e and iPhone Air have USB-C ports but don’t output video over them, so they aren’t supported. Consoles and older Lightning devices need RayNeo’s HDMI adapter.

Both GT Max and GT use dual 1080p Micro-OLED panels, delivering a Full HD image to each eye with ultra-smooth 120Hz refresh rates in 2D mode. GT Max adds 38 pixels per degree, 98% DCI-P3 cinematic color coverage, and TÜV Rheinland triple eye-comfort certification. Each model offers three selectable virtual screen sizes, depending on how immersed you want to be:.

Sources indicate that GT Max’s wider field of view provides a more expansive picture, while GT offers a featherweight design. For travel, the appeal is simple: an immaculate 307-inch personal theater that slips right into your daily bag alongside your Apple gear.

Sources indicate that the GT Series also functions as an instant, private external display for a USB-C Mac. That makes the glasses invaluable far beyond streaming media, especially when you need an expansive, shoulder-surfer-proof dual-monitor workspace on a flight, train, or co-working desk.

Both GT and GT Max include three native 3DoF hardware display modes, meaning you can position your virtual screen around your head:.

It has been revealed that because the tracking runs on dedicated silicon inside the glasses, none of it taxes the Mac or iPhone you’re plugged into. The glasses draw minimal power directly from the connected device and include a four-speaker spatial acoustic array co-tuned by Bang & Olufsen, with a directional Whisper Mode that cuts sound leakage on a plane or in an office.

GT Max also comes in three sizes based on inter-pupillary distance (IPD) — small for under 64mm, medium for 64–67mm, large for over 67mm — ensuring a tailored, comfortable fit.

In a recent development, if an everyday display frame came out of Cupertino today, it would look like RayNeo iO. Rather than heavy visors, iO pairs with your iPhone through the RayNeo app to project glanceable, contextual intelligence into genuine everyday eyewear.

iO uses a high-efficiency binocular MicroLED optical engine to float high-contrast green text into your sightline, presenting a virtual image equivalent to a 33-inch screen viewed from two meters away. With peak eye-level brightness rated at 1,300 nits, reading notes and prompts stays crystal clear even under direct midday sun without occluding your real-world surroundings. The waveguide is 97% transparent and the optical engine is hidden inside the frame, so from the outside these read as ordinary glasses — most people never clock them as smart eyewear at all.

Recent findings suggest that for presentations and pitches, the built-in teleprompter scrolls your notes in sync with your natural speaking cadence, so you keep your eyes locked on your audience instead of looking down at your phone. During face-to-face meetings or international travel, the glasses deliver live subtitles and two-way translation right on the lenses, with support for 55 languages and 109 accents at roughly one second of latency.

Industry observers note that beyond live translation and teleprompting, RayNeo iO acts as a constantly evolving heads-up companion. RayNeo pushes frequent over-the-air (OTA) software updates, continually expanding what the glasses can do throughout your day.

Just now coming to iO is heads-up turn-by-turn navigation, which projects glanceable directional arrows, street names, and real-time transit alerts directly into your line of sight. Whether you’re walking through a new city or cycling down busy streets, you can navigate without holding your iPhone in front of you or looking down at your wrist. Alongside navigation, regular software updates continue to introduce new lifestyle tools, customizable notification filters, and contextual dashboard widgets that keep the hardware feeling fresh.

There’s more coming in December, too: RayNeo is opening the iO SDK to the public, so third-party apps — and community-built ones from people with no development background — start landing on the platform shortly after the holidays.

RayNeo iO’s productivity tools extend that concept further with a focus on personal privacy. This is where they really shine in the Apple ecosystem. Skipping camera modules entirely, the glasses eliminate the social friction of camera-equipped smart eyewear, making them far easier to wear into a boardroom or a client meeting.

A four-microphone array with a bone-conduction sensor captures clear audio for automated meeting minutes and AI summaries that extract key action items. RayNeo V1 and Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite are built in and free out of the box — no subscription required for everyday voice response, contextual reasoning, and ambient assistance. On the temple, an intuitive Smart Crown lets you scroll notifications and highlight key moments with familiar, physical micro-precision.

The titanium frames weigh just 33 grams and are rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, with a battery good for up to two days of typical use, 6.2 hours of continuous live translation, and a 25-minute charge to 80%.

It has been revealed that iO supports Bluetooth 5.4 and carries Apple’s MFi (Made for iPhone) certification. It also has no speakers by design — which sounds like an omission until you realize what it buys you. RayNeo’s ultra-slim titanium temple arms sit flush against your ears and leave them completely free, so your AirPods stay in with Spatial Audio, Transparency Mode, and Active Noise Cancellation untouched for music and calls, while iO handles your heads-up visual intelligence.

When you see a particular price drop, that deal is more likely specific to one or several sellers than to the industry market price across all sellers — depending on their own stock allocations. When that stock is gone, it’s uncertain whether those sellers will have any more units coming in, or even at the same lower price point.

Although more Pokémon cards are being printed than ever in 2026, the Pokémon TCG still has the same problem that sees any readily available selection of packs, or boxes of packs, being sold for above MSRP: There is nowhere near enough supply to meet the demand.

As a result, prices for readily available cards are dictated by market price: estimated by factors like pull rates, the most valuable cards in an expansion, how many print runs an expansion has had, and their overall contribution to the meta.

Day-to-day deals vary between standard Pokémon TCG retailers like Amazon, Walmart, and Target — but the best Black Friday deals are likely to be from third-party sellers operating through those storefronts. There are a lot of sellers competing for sales with one another to offload their stock, and Black Friday is still the ideal season to undercut other Pokémon TCG merchants.
