Apple Watch Series 12 review: Same design, better health tracking, and more listening in

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, looks are deceiving for the latest Apple Watch Series 12.
  • After wearing the Series 12 for the past three-ish weeks, I'm pleased to report that some of these invisible upgrades make a pretty meaningful difference — and that they don't chip away at the watch's battery life.
  • That said, I wouldn't miss half of the upcoming AI-powered "Audio Intelligence" tools if Apple suddenly Thanos-snapped them out of existence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, looks are deceiving for the latest Apple Watch Series 12. On the outside, it appears to be the exact same smartwatch as last year (...and the year before that). But on the inside, it packs redesigned heart rate sensors and a faster S11 chip that enables intriguing new health-tracking features and AI tools, including the Siri AI beta.

After wearing the Series 12 for the past three-ish weeks, I'm pleased to report that some of these invisible upgrades make a pretty meaningful difference — and that they don't chip away at the watch's battery life. My testing found that the Series 12 lasts slightly longer than the Series 11 from fall 2025.

That said, I wouldn't miss half of the upcoming AI-powered "Audio Intelligence" tools if Apple suddenly Thanos-snapped them out of existence. Always-on AI notetakers like Plaud, Pocket, and Bee are a growing trend in Silicon Valley, but they're not for me.

The Series 12's external changes are primarily cosmetic. Apple added a ceramic case option to the mix again, giving buyers a upcoming premium alternative to its aluminum and titanium variants (which now come in new shades like dark bronze and radiant gold). There are some fresh band styles and materials to chew over, too. For testing, Apple sent me a Series 12 with a light gold aluminum case and a sand Sport Band. I'm more of a silver girl myself, but it's very pretty.

Sources indicate that each case type is available in 42mm or 46mm sizes, as usual. They're priced as follows:.

Aluminum case: Starting at $399 with optional cellular connectivity ($100 extra).

Titanium case: Starting at $699 with cellular connectivity.

Ceramic case: Starting at $899 with cellular connectivity.

Recent findings suggest that all of the Series 12's case options are still waterproof for up to 50 meters and carry an IP6X dust resistance rating, but Apple states the glass on the aluminum Series 12 is more durable than before. Otherwise, it's identical to the Series 11 (which was basically identical to the Series 10).

Longtime Apple Watch users who are holding out for an exciting redesign might just stop reading here, understandably. If it's any consolation, we might get one next year. But as someone new to the wearable space, I will say this is a very attractive and comfortable watch. Familiarity breeds contempt, as St. Augustine or Taylor Swift or whomever once mentioned.

Located on the underside of its base, the Series 12's new "Health Sensing System" is a cluster of advanced optical and electrical heart sensors. It has more electrodes that cover a larger surface area for better skin contact during ECG readings, rearranged photodiodes that are better at picking up light, and bigger, more efficient green LEDs that take readings way more frequently.

Sources indicate that while older Apple Watches only logged the user's heart rate continuously during workouts and every five minutes otherwise, the Series 12 now measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day, no matter what you're doing. As proof, these near-real-time readings are available at a glance on a newly introduced heart rate watch face widget, or "complication.".

Sources indicate that the Series 12's fancier sensors also up the frequency of its heart rate variability readings from every two hours to every five minutes. (HRV is a key stress indicator.).

These changes make the Series 12's heart rate data much more precise and detailed than before, and more useful for non-athletes. In turn, other features that use this data should be more accurate, too — Vitals and the Exercise ring, to name a couple. I think this will be the Series 12's biggest selling point for most people.

Industry observers note that apple reworked its pedometer model for the Series 12 to track steps more accurately when your arms are still. It also added a step count complication, aptly called "Steps." That one might not seem like a huge deal, but it actually resolves a common pain point with older Apple Watches: People previously had to DIY a step-count complication by installing a separate pedometer app. It's great to see.

The Series 12 can now produce a "Readiness" score, a 0 to 10 rating of your capacity for physical activity based on your recent exercise, sleep habits, and Vitals. It needs a week of data before it starts working, FYI. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

I like that this score adjusts throughout the day — it's not a one-and-done daily reading. One of my mornings started at a 6 ("Ready") after a decent night's sleep. By the evening that same day, it had fallen to a 4 ("Pace Yourself") because I went on a long, brisk afternoon walk.

Sources indicate that that said, the feature mostly tells me what I could already figure out on my own. I don't necessarily need a score to know I'm less inclined to work out right after exercising. Athletes with more varied training regimens will probably get more value out of this feature than the average person.

The Series 12's four Audio Intelligence features use its built-in microphone to pick up on sounds and conversations. To address privacy concerns, Apple indicates it has ensured it doesn't create or store any recordings and that the raw audio is completely inaccessible before it's deleted. And if you're really weirded out by them, you can just opt out.

Music Recognition with Shazam now works automatically. It usually takes only a couple of seconds to identify a song, depending on the amount of background noise, and it's always spot-on.

Sound Recognition can alert you to sounds such as sirens, doorbells, smoke alarms, barking dogs, and car horns. It liked to confuse a train's "door closing" chime for an appliance bell, but was otherwise accurate in my testing. It's a useful addition for people who are deaf and hard of hearing.

According to recent reports, live Rewind transcribes the tail end of a recent conversation when you double-press the Series 12's dial (aka "Digital Crown"). Apple notes it can show the last 15 seconds of speech, but in practice it's closer to 10 seconds. Either way, it feels kind of pointless. It's such a short window of time that you might as well just ask the person you're chatting with to repeat themselves. It's also not correct 100 percent of the time. It once confused the phrase "pencil me in" for "Pennsylvania.".

According to recent reports, finally, there's Siri Recap, which is essentially a built-in AI notetaker. (It's meant for oral conversations, but it's also summarized TikToks I've watched and phone calls I've taken on speaker mode.) Its outlines are pretty macro and vary in their helpfulness depending on the conversation. I found it really good for recapping food orders and reviewing topics discussed in my Italian classes, but a little clunky when it comes to casual conversations. It doesn't distinguish between different speakers and sometimes mashes topics together. It's also not completely accurate — it remarked a friend named their baby "Popsicle" (no <3) — but it seems to be improving as I've continued to use it.

Sources indicate that I struggle with Siri Recap the most because it makes me feel like a creep. It doesn't alert you when it's listening in on a conversation, much less the person(s) you're speaking with, so it's on you to tell them that you're documenting your private discussions for later reference. (Awkward!) Keep in mind that such admissions will likely change the nature of your interactions: People edit themselves and put up their guards when they know they're being watched.

Apple rated the Series 12 for up to 24 hours of battery life, but in my testing, it's offered around 45 to 51 hours of normal use per charge. (Crucially, I haven't needed to activate Low Power Mode to hit those numbers.) This is a real testament to the S11 chip's power efficiency. It's also a nice bump from the Series 11, which Mashable's Stan Schroeder described as "a one-and-a-half-day smartwatch.".

According to recent reports, apple says the Series 12 charges faster than its predecessor, too. I don't have a Series 11 handy to verify that, but I've been impressed with the Series 12's charging speed. Right before going to bed one night, I realized it didn't have enough charge for sleep tracking, which requires at least 30 percent battery. Luckily, just five minutes on an outlet bumped it from 23 to 39 percent battery.

With its latest mainstream smartwatch, Apple refines a familiar design with near-live heart rate tracking, noticeable battery-life gains, and a step-tracking widget — a small but welcome quality-of-life tweak. Audio Intelligence, meanwhile, takes a back seat to these more meaningful improvements.

For most people, the Series 12 is the best Apple Watch to buy right now (unless, of course, you're willing to wait for next year's redesign). It's an easy recommendation over the more expensive Apple Watch Ultra 4, which offers much of the same functionality but adds longer battery life and enhanced durability for outdoor and endurance activities. Compared to the budget-friendly Apple Watch SE 3, the Series 12 is also a more future-proof choice, with a considerably more comprehensive suite of health and fitness tracking features to boot.

Topics Apple Apple Watch Smartwatches.

Bass Pro Shops and Cabela’s — The first 250 customers (ages 16 and older) at every store will receive a free mystery gift card worth $10 to $500, which will be valid from Dec. 6 to 24.

JCPenney — Select stores are giving away four prizes throughout the day, including a miniature Harry Potter snow globe, a Ninja air fryer, diamond earrings, and a Samsonite suitcase.

Michaels — Every store is giving away 500 "Countdown to Craftsmas" advent calendars. One calendar in every store contains a $100 gift card, and one recipient will win a $10,000 grand prize.

Sephora at Kohl's — The first 200 customers at select stores will receive a free Kohl’s Cash voucher worth $5 to $100 to spend on beauty purchases that day.

In a recent development, target — The first 100 customers at every store will receive a free Target gift card worth $25, $50, or $100. One person per store will get a $1,000 gift card.

In a recent development, paying for a membership just to shop a sale feels a little counterproductive. Luckily, eligible customers can try Amazon Prime free for 30 days. After the trial, Prime costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, depending on your selected proposal.

Sources indicate that prime comes with more than free shipping, though that’s probably the perk you’ll use most while shopping for gifts. You also get Prime Video, Amazon Music’s ad-free listening options, access to a selection of books through Prime Reading, and member-exclusive deals. The newest addition is $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon — a useful extra for the nights you’d rather order dinner than make it.

Deezer Family — One month free, then $19.99 per month. Cancel anytime.

According to recent reports, not all reading has to involve sitting down with a book. Audible’s 30-day free trial lets new customers choose one audiobook from its collection, including bestsellers and new releases, and listen to an included catalog of podcasts. After the trial, it automatically renews at $8.99 per month unless you cancel.

There’s also a separate promotion for three months at $0.99 per month, plus a $20 Audible bonus. I wouldn’t call that free, but paying $2.97 for three months might make more sense than taking one free month and then paying the regular rate.

It has been revealed that hoopla — Free through participating public libraries. Check whether your library offers access before signing up; this is library borrowing, not a subscription trial that turns into a monthly bill.

Kobo Plus Listen — 14 days free, then $7.99 per month. The Read & Listen plan includes both ebooks and audiobooks for $9.99 per month after the trial. You can use the Kobo Books app on your phone or tablet, so there’s no need to buy an e-reader.

According to recent reports, everand — 30 days free, with plans starting at $11.99 per month afterward. The trial includes one premium-title unlock, plus unlimited access to a separate catalog of more than 20,000 audiobooks, ebooks, and podcasts.

According to recent reports, all You Can Books — 30 days free, then $24.99 per month. The service advertises unlimited downloads from its catalog of audiobooks, ebooks, language courses, and other content, and claims downloaded files remain yours even after cancellation.

I’d use the free month to check whether the publications you actually want to read are included. A long list of magazines sounds nice, but it doesn’t mean much if you’re only opening one of them.

After the trial, the subscription costs $14.99 per month, so it's worth setting a reminder to cancel if you don't plan on keeping it.

If you've been thinking about switching phone providers, Verizon is also offering a 30-day free trial, giving you a chance to test its network without switching providers. You can keep your existing phone number and continue using your current network while trying Verizon through an eSIM. There's no credit card required, no contract, and no need to remember to cancel, either. The trial automatically expires after 30 days, so you won't be charged if you decide not to switch.

Sources indicate that T-Mobile — 30 days free for eligible non-T-Mobile customers with a compatible, unlocked device. Includes access to T-Mobile's network, satellite coverage, and member benefits, with no credit card, credit check, or commitment required.

Visible — 15 days free with unlimited data, talk, text, and hotspot access on Verizon's network. No credit card, contract, or automatic renewal required.

AT&T Wireless — 30 days free with unlimited talk and text, plus 100GB of data. Keep your current phone, number, and service while testing the network. Compatible iPhone or Android required.

And if you're planning to pick up a newly introduced Apple device during the Black Friday sales, you could get an even better deal, with three months free when you purchase an eligible device.

Glo — 7 days free, with access to more than 12,000 on-demand yoga, Pilates, meditation, and strength classes led by over 60 instructors.

Peloton App — Free trial for new members, with access to thousands of workout classes across more than 15 exercise types, including options that don't require equipment. Cancel anytime.

In a recent development, ladder — 7 days free, with access to all training plans, personalized workout recommendations, introductory classes, and fitness communities. No payment information required to start the trial.

Nike Training Club — Completely free, with access to guided workouts, multi-week training programs, and fitness advice. No subscription or trial period required.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a way to unwind after a busy day, Calm is offering a seven-day free trial of its Premium membership. You'll get access to more than 50,000 minutes of content, including guided meditations, Sleep Stories, relaxing music, and nature sounds. After the trial, the subscription automatically renews at $79.99 per year, plus applicable taxes, so make sure you cancel before the seven days are up if you don't want to continue.

If you're a sports fan seeking a Black Friday streaming deal, Fox One is your best option this year.

What exactly does a Fox One subscription get you? A whole lot of sports, including live Sunday afternoon NFL games, Massive Ten college football matchups, college basketball, MLB, NASCAR, and the list goes on. Sure, a month of streaming isn't that long, but you'll get access to a surprising number of games. This week alone would grant you access to the Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving Day game, West Virginia vs. Utah on Black Friday, in-market college football on Saturday, and in-market Sunday afternoon NFL games.

When you're not watching live sports, Fox One also unlocks your local Fox station and Fox Entertainment on demand, including movies, TV shows (like MasterChef and The Simpsons), and a bunch more. For $4.99, it's certainly worth a shot. Just remember to cancel before the month is up if you want to avoid the full charge. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we've all been wrecked by the global memory crisis, aka RAMageddon, this year. Hard drives, microSD cards, portable SSDs, and other tech essentials have been rapidly rising in price, and there's no sign of that upward trajectory slowing any time soon. In fact, experts warn that things are going to get worse before they get better. Yikes.

Whether you've been wanting to build out your PC, secure offline data backups, or give your console a little breathing space, Black Friday is the best time to take advantage of portable SSD and hard drive deals. Compared to prices we saw in early November, these deals are considerably better. We'll be tracking all of the best SSD deals from brands like SanDisk, Lexar, Samsung, Western Digital (WD_Black), and beyond leading up to and throughout Cyber Week. Here are our top Black Friday picks.

It has been revealed that mashable's sister site PCMag gave the Samsung 990 Pro internal SSD an "Excellent" rating in their in-depth review, highlighting its zippy read and write speeds up to 6,900 MB/s. That makes it a solid choice for large game installs, video editing, 3D work, data-heavy projects, and other creative tasks. It's compatible with PlayStation 5, includes Samsung Magician software, and offers 256-bit AES hardware-based encryption. We'll be keeping an eye on its price heading into Black Friday, but you can already grab it for much less than usual at under $400 for 2TB. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Industry observers note that the SanDisk Extreme Fit USB-C flash drive with 1TB of storage is on a major discount. SanDisk lists the price at $312.99, making the Amazon sale price of $203.99 a 35% discount.

SanDisk says this is their smallest high-capacity USB-C flash drive, and it sits so close to flush with your laptop that you won't need to remove it every time. Plus, it has read speeds of up to 400 MB/s.

According to recent reports, coming with an official license from Nintendo, the SanDisk microSD Express Card is a must-have accessory for the Switch 2. You'll have ample space to keep your favorite game titles conveniently in one location. The 512GB card comes with write and read speeds that'll be great for your holiday and winter gaming needs.

It has been revealed that wading through the deals on iPads, MacBooks, and AirPods, it's tough to ignore T-Mobile's massive sale on iPhones. If you've been waiting until now to upgrade, you're in luck: For limited-time, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free at T-Mobile. Yes, you read that right.

T-Mobile keeps things surprisingly flexible when it comes to qualifying for this Black Friday deal. You can port your existing phone number from an eligible rival carrier to a qualifying T-Mix plan, and T-Mobile covers the full cost of the phone. Alternatively, existing customers can trade in an eligible phone in any condition on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

According to recent reports, T-Mobile distributes the full discount as 36 monthly bill credits. If you leave T-Mobile or cancel your line before that three-year payment strategy ends, the credits stop immediately, and you will owe the remaining balance on the device.

You are also still required to pay local sales tax on the phone's full $1,199 retail value upfront, plus T-Mobile's standard $35 device connection fee per line at checkout. Unfortunately, you can't escape those upfront charges.

Score the Apple iPhone 18 Pro for free with T-Mobile over Black Friday.

On Friday, Nov. 27, the retailer is selling a $100 Best Buy gift card for $60 — essentially handing out $40 in free spending money toward your next tech upgrade or holiday gift.

According to recent reports, that works out to a 40% discount on future Best Buy purchases, which can easily stack with existing Black Friday sale prices. Because quantities are limited and there are a few rules in place, here is everything you need to know before you head out on Friday morning.

You have to use the $100 gift card on a separate transaction, which just means buying the card first and immediately putting that $100 toward your next Black Friday pickup — like a new TV, laptop, or holiday gift.

In a recent development, purchases made from Oct. 30 through Dec. 31, 2026 are covered by Best Buy's Holiday Price Match Guarantee and are eligible for extended returns through Jan. 15, 2027 (excluding cell phones, AppleCare+ plans, and holiday decor).

If you are mapping out a full-morning route, browse our rundown of Black Friday 2026 opening times before heading out (and confirm your local store's hours, just in case). You will also want to set up your free My Best Buy account ahead of time so checkout goes smoothly.

One of the biggest shopping events of the year is finally here: Black Friday.

Recent findings suggest that early Black Friday deals started rolling in weeks ago, but now we're well into the official sales. Yes, instead of standing in a cold line at 4 a.m. the day after Thanksgiving, we get to shop online under cozy blankets while watching Christmas movies.

Recent findings suggest that since the deals between retailers can feel overwhelming, it's good to head into the mega-sale event with a proposal. From knowing when sales from retailers like Amazon and Best Buy start to knowing which products will likely go on sale to preparing your own shopping list, we've got you covered on everything you need to know to shop Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

This year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27, but that date isn't all that crucial these days. Almost every major retailers has already started official Black Friday sales. We expect to see some special deals drop on Nov. 27, but if you're looking to shop Black Friday sales, it's your time to shine.

Sources indicate that absolutely yes. The mega-retailer's sale kicked off Thursday, Nov. 19 — more info on the full date range of the sale is below. Expect deals on everything from the year's top tech to home essentials. Naturally, Amazon's devices also get markdowns across the board. So far, the retailer has teased the following:.

Save up to 45% on Amazon's 2024 Kindle Colorsoft, 55-inch Ember Artline TV, and 55-inch Ember Mini LED-Series TV.

Save up to 50% on select headphones and speakers from Sony, Beats, JBL, Marshall, and Sonos.

Save up to 40% on select Ninja appliances, including the Creami, Foodi, and Slushi.

Save up to 40% on select iRobot and Bissell floorcare.

Save up to $500 on select Balsam Hill and Fraser Hill Farm artificial Christmas trees.

Sources indicate that amazon: Amazon's Black Friday sale runs from Thursday, Nov. 19 to Nov. 30, offering 12 consecutive days of deals. Each day of the sale will feature "Today's Substantial Deals," where select products will be on sale for up to 60% off, except for on Black Friday and Cyber Monday proper. One batch of deals will go live at 3 a.m. ET, while another will go on sale at 11 a.m. ET.

According to recent reports, best Buy: Black Friday at Best Buy starts on Nov. 19, and runs through Saturday, Nov. 28. Its Cyber Monday sale runs from Nov. 29 to Nov. 30, with a Cyber Week sale that extends savings from Dec. 1 to Dec. 6. Total and Plus members of the My Best Buy program are also eligible to earn double points on their purchases from Nov. 19 to Dec. 6.

Walmart: Walmart has three major sale events throughout November: the early Black Friday sale from Nov. 12 to Nov. 15, the Black Friday sale from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26), and the online-only Cyber Monday sale from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

Target: Target's first Early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 5 to Nov. 7. From Nov. 1 to Dec. 24, Target's Deal of the Day offer kicks off, featuring fresh deals every day. Every weekend after Nov. 7, the retailer will also drop new limited-time holiday offers.

Considering prices went up this year on pretty much Apple devices except for AirPods, Black Friday will be the time to pick up upcoming Apple devices. The short answer: Apple products will absolutely be on sale this Black Friday. The slightly longer answer: the best place to pick up Apple products during Black Friday sales will be at retailers like Amazon, Walmart, or Best Buy, which often duke it out to see who will drop a MacBook or pair of AirPods to the record-low price first (or, more impressively, keep it in stock the longest). Already in the lead-up, MacBooks are $250 off, and the AirPods Pro 3 are $100 off.

In a recent development, as for Apple itself holding Black Friday sales, the Apple Store features its own Black Friday sale every year: a free gift card for future use with the purchase of select devices. We expect to see the same this year, so we recommend picking up your Apple devices elsewhere if you're looking to save as much cash as possible.

It has been revealed that target has great Black Friday deals if you're looking for toys, Lego sets, Christmas decor, books, or small kitchen appliances. Target's Deal of the Day offers extra savings on hot items, and you can preview upcoming deals several days before they happen, giving shoppers time to set a reminder.

Industry observers note that walmart doesn't skimp on Black Friday deals, and they tend to compete with the best Amazon sales, like $149 Apple AirPods Pro 3. According to recent reports, officially, Walmart's Black Friday deals are live through Nov. 29, followed by Cyber Monday from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2. If a deal you were hoping to grab at Amazon sells out, it's always worth checking stock at Walmart.

Best Buy gets in on the sale action, and it's worth paying close attention to the retailer's doorbuster deals which offer ridiculous savings but tend to sell out rapidly (R.I.P $149.99 Ninja Slushi). Like Walmart, Best Buy tends to price-match Amazon deals. If you wind up needing a gift in a hurry, Best Buy tends to offer great in-store pickup options as well as quick shipping.

It has been revealed that while Black Friday brings many of the best prices of the year, it's not the end-all, be-all for every product out there. According to Google-analyzed holiday trends, fancy cookware and suitcases hit their lowest prices in late December, while tech like TVs and gaming consoles are likely to hit their lowest prices during Black Friday and Cyber Week (with the latter seeing one final dip right before Christmas).

There can be some variance from category to category, so we recommend keeping track of Mashable's deals coverage. Our team has been covering Black Friday (and deals in general) for nearly a decade, so we can tell your firsthand whether or not a product is worth grabbing during the height of sales.

Sources indicate that with Black Friday proper bringing some of the lowest prices, what deals are worth shopping now? It's an especially relevant question in 2026, a year that saw many historic price increases across everything from laptops to Kindles. In other words, shopping smart has never been a smarter decision, which is why we've gathered some of the best early Black Friday savings so far.

It has been revealed that the more apt question is what doesn't go on sale during Black Friday. That's to say, if there's a product you're looking to grab on sale, whether that be a new TV or paper towels, Black Friday is the time to do it.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the deals we have listed above, we expect to see more savings on MacBooks, Windows laptops, video games and consoles, robot vacuums, regular stick vacuums, drones, trading cards, books, board games, and power tools. This list is by no means exhaustive — if there's a good deal worth writing up, you'll likely find it in our deals coverage.

The best Black Friday deals generally last through Cyber Monday, which falls on Nov. 30 this year. Some deals do linger through the week, and some Cyber Monday sales (such as Walmart's) are scheduled to extend beyond Cyber Monday proper. And as Target's deal-of-the-day sale demonstrates, there are almost always Black Friday-worthy sales through essentially Christmas. That said, for the best shot at scoring big savings (and for catching a deal while it's still available), shopping during Black Friday weekend is typically a good rule of thumb.

Sources indicate that amazon and Walmart don't offer a price-matching policy. Best Buy's Holiday Price Match Guarantee offers price matches against itself through Jan. 15, 2027 on products purchased from Oct. 30 to Dec. 31. Target used to offer price matching against other retailers during the holidays, but now its policy resembles Best Buy's: Target shoppers who made a purchase on or after Nov. 1 in person or online can request a price match if they spot a drop on or before Dec. 24.
